subject: Temporary carve-out & autoscale exception request for Q4 partner launch
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-24T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: temporary carve-out for BrightHealth Q4 pilot (Nov 29 - Dec 13)

Team —

Quick heads-up / ask. BrightHealth (pilot customer, see HS-Deal-123456) confirmed a targeted feature launch during the first two weeks of the holiday window: Nov 29 -> Dec 13. Their Ops team is expecting a ~3.5–4x uptick in inference concurrency for the first 72 hours of the pilot, with elevated but tapering traffic thereafter. They will send production traffic to our Dedicated endpoint.

We need a short-term capacity guarantee for this window to hit their SLA expectations. Specifically I’m asking for:
- A temporary dedicated carve-out (opaque pool) sized to handle peak ~180 concurrent users across the session-heavy workflow (estimate in attached q4-launch-mcap.xlsx).
- An autoscale policy exception so the carve-out is not preempted by cross-tenant autoscaling / pooling heuristics; we still want normal scaling outside the carve-out.
- A pinned model variant for the window (Rishi: can you confirm which variant?) and rollback/fallback rules.

We can offer BrightHealth a 30% credit for the two-week reservation or apply it as a committed credit from their pilot terms (Karthik, pls coordinate commercial).

Please see attached traffic-curve.csv and the MCAP workbook. Can we get a feasibility check by EOD tomorrow? If possible, include rough cost delta + operational runbook (who paged, who owns failover).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Revenue
Redwood Inference

Attachments: q4-launch-mcap.xlsx (spreadsheet), traffic-curve.csv (csv)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary carve-out for BrightHealth Q4 pilot (Nov 29 - Dec 13)

Marissa —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifying items before we size the carve-out:
1) Target GPU type: are we ok to use mixed ND/Xeon + A100 (6x A100 equiv)? If BrightHealth requires specific latency SLOs we may need A100p.
2) Expected average token/second per session and peak concurrent sessions (the MCAP has a range; I want a single best-estimate number to model queueing).
3) Are we allowed to temporarily relax cluster-wide CPU/eviction thresholds for the carve-out, or do you want the carve-out strictly isolated?

If answers come back quickly I can run the simulation and give a recommended pool size + cost delta by EOD Nov 25.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Capacity & Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary carve-out for BrightHealth Q4 pilot (Nov 29 - Dec 13)

Adding model constraints.

Marissa — based on the feature described, the team plans to serve the "redwood-2-realtime" variant (fp16, 8-bit quant option). Latency SLO target is 200–300ms median for short sessions; 95th <= 700ms. If we pin to redwood-2-realtime-qa (pruned KV caches), we can reduce GPU memory and multiplex more requests into the pool, which reduces required GPUs by ~20% vs the full variant. I attached a quick sketch in carveout-impact.pdf.

If product can accept the 8-bit quant option and the slightly higher tail latency under load, we can probably get away with 3x A100 for peak instead of 4x. However, we need explicit sign-off from BrightHealth on the model variant (Karthik / Laura — can you confirm with them?)

Also: we should pin the model version and disable live model-swap rollouts for the window — that prevents surprise perf regressions.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML — Serving
Redwood Inference

Attachment: carveout-impact.pdf (analysis)

Hi Team at BrightHealth —

Thanks again for the call earlier. To finalize internal sizing we need a confirmation of the expected traffic curve. Per our simulation we see three options: conservative (30% lower than your original), expected (as attached), and aggressive (+25%). Can you confirm which curve you expect to bring for Nov 29 start?

We are proposing the following commercial offset: Redwood will apply a 30% usage credit for the two-week carve-out window in exchange for your agreement to a short termination notice (48 hours) in case cross-region emergencies require reallocation. Please confirm by EOD Nov 26.

Thanks —

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-29T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary carve-out & autoscale exception request for Q4 pilot (implementation notes)

Pulling together the operational plan. TL;DR: feasible with small infra work.

Plan outline:
- Create a temporary tenant-isolated pool ("bh-q4-carveout") of 4x A100 GPUs (can reduce to 3x if BrightHealth signs off on quantized variant).
- Autoscaler exception: add an override flag to the placement controller so pool nodes are only considered for non-preemptible allocations. Duration: 2026-11-29T00:00 to 2026-12-13T23:59 (UTC).
- Model pin: enforce config in the control plane to block model version rollouts and disable auto-upgrade on that pool.
- Fallback: traffic will spill to "redwood-dedicated-fallback" with 10s retry/backoff, and we will route on latency > 800ms.
- Runbook: on-call (Dev) -> escalate to Hannah -> notify Marissa & Karthik. I’ll add a short playbook to the incident runbook repo.

Estimated infra delta (cost): ~$28k for the two weeks at list. With the 30% credit that Karthik proposed, net impact to BrightHealth will be ~$19.6k; Redwood is covering ~$8.4k as credit.

I will provision the pool once I get greenlight from Hannah + commercial confirmation from Karthik.

Dev Patel
Engineering (Serving)
Redwood Inference
